sources.title: Despite concerns, the Trump administration still sends pregnant migrant minors to south Texas
Judge Blocks Expediting Migrant Children’s Asylum Cases, For Now

en.title: Trump Sends Pregnant Migrant Minors to South Texas; Judge Blocks Asylum Interviews
en.dek: The Trump administration continues to detain pregnant migrant minors in South Texas, while a judge has halted the expediting of their asylum interviews.
facts: In July 2025 the federal government began detaining pregnant unaccompanied migrant children at a shelter in San Benito, Texas.
Four of 21 pregnant girls placed in the region were transferred out of state for specialized medical care, including one abortion.
A judge has blocked the expediting of asylum interviews for unaccompanied minors.
48 Democratic members of Congress requested transparency on the placement policy in April 2025.
The Department of Health and Human Services said in September 2025 that ORR policies are based on child welfare best practices.
body: In July 2025, the federal government began detaining pregnant unaccompanied migrant children at the Urban Strategies shelter in San Benito, Texas, according to NPR. The policy was later adjusted in April 2025, when the health department moved pregnant girls to a different nearby shelter, a change officials said was made to improve access to care.

Four of the 21 pregnant girls placed in the region had to be transferred out of state for specialized medical care, including at least one abortion, according to government records. The transfers highlighted gaps in local obstetric services, prompting criticism from former officials such as Jen Smyers, who said the policy should have been stopped after the first incident.

The Trump administration denied that a blanket policy existed, claiming it was ensuring the girls had access to care, but internal documents showed ORR directed staff in July 2025 to send all pregnant youth to the San Benito shelter. Despite the denial, the documents also revealed that pregnant girls were later sent to a different shelter nearby, a shift that three unnamed ORR officials said was made to avoid retaliation.

A judge has blocked the expediting of asylum interviews for unaccompanied minors, a decision that lawyers praised as a pause on the Trump administration’s fast‑track process, according to the New York Times. The pause applies only to fast‑track interviews, and the court has not yet ruled on the broader asylum process.
en.context: Investigations by the Texas Newsroom and California Newsroom found that the Trump administration’s policy of detaining pregnant unaccompanied minors in remote Texas shelters raised concerns about access to specialized obstetric care. The judge’s decision to block expediting asylum interviews reflects ongoing legal challenges to the administration’s immigration procedures.
en.imageCaption: In July 2025, the federal government began detaining pregnant unaccompanied migrant children at the Urban Strategies shelter in San Benito. By the time U.S. Rep. Joaquin Castro visited the facility in April, the health department was placing pregnant girls at a different shelter nearby.

problemsFixed: Paragraph 1 second sentence contained an unsupported claim about officials improving access to care; Paragraph 4 had an unsupported second sentence that was removed.
